Chapter 2.  Admission

Paragraph 1   Admission to Bachelor’s degree program

Article 2.1  Scope of application

This paragraph applies to Bachelor’s programs.

Article 2.2  Admission request

1. With the admission request, the candidate provides the information and documents listed on the web page.

2. A request for admission to an English-taught program will not be considered until all required documents have been submitted. With respect to a request for admission to an English-taught study program on the basis of a colloquium doctum as referred to in Article 2.9 , all documents required may be submitted up to one day before the start of the degree program.

3. A certificate of admission to the Bachelor's program is issued by or on behalf of the institutional board.

Article 2.3  Further previous education requirements and deficiencies

1. For admission based on a VWO diploma to a Bachelor’s program listed in Appendix 2 Profiles and courses (Article 2.3), the candidate has the profile or subject listed therein.

2. A candidate who holds a VWO diploma without the profiles or subjects referred to in Appendix 2 Profiles and courses (Article 2.3) , or has an exemption from the previous education requirement of the VWO diploma as referred to in article 2.4,  may remedy this deficiency by:

a. Obtaining the relevant Boswell-Beta certificate;

b. Passing the relevant State Examination and examination at the Central Entrance Examination Committees (CCVX);

c. - d. does not apply in this document.

e. Repealed.

f. does not apply in this document.

f. For the Bachelor Cognitive Science and Artificial Intelligence (CSAI):

- obtaining the relevant Boswell-Beta certificate; passing the relevant State examination and the examination at the Central Committees Preliminary Examination (CCVX); 

- in accordance with article 2.4. paragraph 2, only for students with a non-Dutch previous education: achieving a minimum score of 70% on the Online Mathematics Placement Test (OMPT) - level A insofar as the deficiency concerns the further preliminary mathematics A or B requirements.

g. For the Bachelor Liberal Arts and Sciences (LAS):

In order to be admitted to the Bachelor’s program in Liberal Arts and Sciences, the student must receive a positive final judgment from the Admissions Board. 

The Admissions Board considers the following criteria to form a final judgment: 

• the candidate possesses, in the judgment of the Admissions Board, sufficient motivation and intellectual ability to meet the final requirements of the program; 

• the candidate has sufficient command of the English language, as referred to in
Article 2.6; 

• the candidate has, in the opinion of the Admissions Board, sufficient interest in multi- and
interdisciplinarity; 

• the candidate has, in the opinion of the Admissions Board, sufficient international orientation; 

• the candidate has, in the opinion of the Admissions Board, performed sufficient relevant extra-curricular activities; 

• the candidate has, in the opinion of the Admissions Board, the attitude and communication skills to function properly in an international classroom.

3. Repealed.

Article 2.4  Exemptions from the previous education requirement of secondary pre-university education (VWO)

1. The previous education requirement of a VWO diploma does not apply to the candidate who has:

a. A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree;(17)

b. At least an equivalent diploma as referred to in Article 7.28, paragraphs 1 and 2 of the Act;(18)

c. A propaedeutic certificate from an accredited program in Dutch higher professional education, or a certificate from a college of higher education on completion of all educational components this program.

d. A propaedeutic certificate from an accredited program in Dutch university education, or a statement from a university on the completion of all educational components of the first year of this program.

e. proof of admission for the previous year of study of the relevant program.

2. The exemption in the first paragraph relates only to the previous education requirement of the VWO diploma. For admission to the degree program, the candidate demonstrates knowledge and skills in the profiles or subjects listed in Appendix 2. The regulations on deficiencies in Article 2.3, paragraph 2 apply.

Article 2.5  Dutch language proficiency

1. For admission to a Bachelor’s program for which the language of instruction according to Article 3.3, paragraph 2, under b (19) is Dutch, the candidate has an adequate command of the Dutch language.(20) This is demonstrated by a pre-university education certificate (VWO diploma) or an equivalent non-Dutch diploma as referred to in Article 1.4 of the Regulations governing the Application and Admission to Higher Education.

2. The person who does not have a certificate as mentioned in Article 2.5, paragraph 1 demonstrates sufficient command of the Dutch language by means of a diploma or a certificate demonstrating successful completion of:

  1. a propaedeutic examination of a program with Dutch as the language of instruction from a university or university of applied sciences education;

  2. a pre-Master’s program with Dutch as the language of instruction;

  3. a Bachelor’s degree from a program of a university or a university of applied sciences with Dutch as the language of instruction;

  4. Secondary Education Diploma, specialization General Secondary Education;

  5. Zeugnis der allgemeinen Hochschulreife under the condition that up to and including the final examination year the subject Dutch has been taken;

  6. Dutch as a Foreign Language in the profile Language Proficiency Higher Education ;

  7. State examination in Dutch as a Second Language, program II; 

  8. Interuniversity Language Test of Dutch for Speakers of Other Languages (ITNA), B2 or higher;

  9. International Baccalaureate (IB) or European Baccalaureate (EB) under the condition that the subject of Dutch has been followed, up to and including the final examination year;

  10. not applicable. (21)

3. does not apply in this document.

Article 2.6  English language skills

1. For admission to a Bachelor’s program for which the language of instruction is English according to Article 3.3, paragraph 2, under b, (23)a general CEFR (Common European Framework of Reference) level of B2 has been established. The candidate demonstrates satisfactory command of the English language at this level by means of a previous education program or a certificate (24) with the following scores:

  1. TOEFL iBT on the scale score used by TOEFL until January 2026 (not the TOEFL Essentials and not the TOEFL iBT Home Edition) with a minimum total score of 80 and a minimum sub score of 17 for Speaking and 19 for Writing;
  2. TOEFL iBT at the scale score used by TOEFL as of January 2026 (not the TOEFL Essentials and not the TOEFL iBT Home Edition) with a minimum total score of 4.5 and a minimum sub score of 4 for Speaking and 4 for Writing;
  3. Academic IELTS with an average minimum score of 6.0 and no lower than 5.5 for Speaking and Writing; or
  4. Cambridge B2 First, C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency  with a score of at least 173 average and a minimum sub score for Speaking and Writing of 160.

2. The language certificate is not older than two calendar years at the date of application.

3. Moved.

4. In exceptional cases, the Examination Board may decide that the English language proficiency of the candidate meets the scores mentioned in the first paragraph, without explicitly submitting a certificate indicating successful completion.

5. Repealed.

Article 2.7  Exemption of English language proficiency certificates

1. A certificate referred to in Article 2.6 is not required of a candidate for a joint program or a dual degree, insofar as it follows from the cooperation agreement for the program between the participating institutions.

2. A certificate referred to in Article 2.6 is not required of an applicant who has a:

  1. VWO diploma or a partial certificate in English at the VWO final examination level;

  2. diploma as referred to in Article 1.4 of the Regulations on Application and Admission to Higher Education with an English language proficiency level equivalent to that of VWO;

  3. International Baccalaureate (IB) diploma with an English language proficiency level equivalent to VWO;

  4. European Baccalaureate (EB) diploma with an English language proficiency level equivalent to VWO;

  5. diploma of a propaedeutic year of a program in Dutch higher education, or a certificate from a Dutch university of applied sciences or university on the completion of all educational components of the first year of this program with English as the language of instruction;

  6. diploma from one of the following previous education programs that have been deemed equivalent by the Nuffic, or on the basis of existing treaties of the Netherlands, or on the basis of standing practice within Tilburg University with respect to diploma valuation, with an English language proficiency level of VWO, in which the subject of English has been obtained with a pass on the final exam:

The student submits supporting documents on the basis of which the student requests an exemption from submitting a certificate of English language proficiency;
  8. Bachelor's or Master's degree from a higher education degree program, issued by a university or university of applied sciences in the Netherlands;

Not applicable.

Paragraph 2  Admission to Master’s degree programs

Article 2.14  Scope of application

This section applies to Master’s degree programs.

Article 2.15  Proof of admission

1. Proof of admission is required to enroll in a Master's program.

2. does not apply in this document.

3. A certificate of admission is issued by the Admissions Board on behalf of the Dean . (31) If necessary, it seeks advice from the coordinator of the program in question before issuing it.

Article 2.16  Admission request

1. A request for admission to the program may be submitted to the Admissions Board  from October 1 until the deadline stated on the website. A request for admission to an English-taught Master’s program (which includes an English-taught Research Master's program) will not be considered until all documents required for this purpose have been submitted.

2. For admission, the Admissions Board shall conduct an assessment of the candidate's knowledge, understanding, and skills. In addition to written evidence of previous education, the Examination Board may have certain knowledge and skills tested by experts in or outside the university.

3. - 4. does not apply in this document.

Article 2.17  Previous education

A candidate is admissible to the Master’s program if the candidate:

  1. holds a diploma required for admission to the program in accordance with Appendix 3 Previous education for admission to a Master's degree (Article 2.17) to these Regulations; and
  2. meets the qualitative requirements listed in Appendix 3 Previous education for admission to a Master's degree (Article 2.17) to these Regulations for the degree program for which such requirements are set.

Article 2.18  Dutch language proficiency

For admission to a Master’s program for which the language of instruction is Dutch, the candidate must have sufficient command of the Dutch language. Article 2.5 applies by analogy.

Article 2.19  English language proficiency

1. For admission to a Master's program for which the language of instruction is English according to Article 3.3, paragraph 2, under b, a general CEFR (Common European Framework of Reference) level of C1 has been established. The candidate demonstrates adequate command of the English language at this level by means of a diploma from a previous education program or language certificate with the following scores: 

  1. TOEFL iBT on the scale score used by TOEFL until January 2026 (not the TOEFL Essentials and not the TOEFL iBT Home Edition) with a minimum total score of 90 and a minimum sub score of 21 for Speaking and 22 for Writing;
  2. TOEFL iBT at the scale score used by TOEFL as of January 2026 (not the TOEFL Essentials and not the TOEFL iBT Home Edition) with a minimum total score of 5 and a minimum sub score of 5 for Speaking and 5 for Writing;
  3. Academic IELTS with an average minimum score of 6.5 and no lower than 6.0 for Speaking and Writing; or
  4. Cambridge C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency with a score of at least 180 average and a minimum sub score for Speaking and Writing of 180.

2. For admission to a Research Master's program for which the language of instruction is English according to Article 3.3, paragraph 2, under b, a general CEFR (Common European Framework of Reference) level C1+ has been established. The candidate demonstrates adequate command of the English language by means of a diploma from a previous education program or language certificate with the following scores:

  1. TOEFL iBT on the scale score used by TOEFL until January 2026  (not the TOEFL Essentials and not the TOEFL iBT Home Edition) with a minimum total score of 100 and a minimum sub score of 21 for Speaking and 25 for Writing;
  2. TOEFL iBT at the scale score used by TOEFL as of January 2026 (not the TOEFL Essentials and not the TOEFL iBT Home Edition) with a minimum overall score of 5.5 and a minimum sub score of 5 for Speaking and 5 for Writing;
  3. Academic IELTS with a minimum average score of 7,0 and no lower than 6.5 for Speaking and Writing; or
  4. Cambridge C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency with a score of at least 193 average and a minimum sub score for Speaking and Writing of 185.

3. The language certificate is not older than two calendar years at the date of application. 

4. Moved.

Article 2.20  Exemption of English language proficiency certificates

1. A certificate referred to in Article 2.19 is not required of a candidate for a joint program or a dual degree, insofar as it follows from the cooperation agreement for the program between the participating institutions.

2. A certificate as referred to in Article 2.19 is not required of a candidate who holds: 

a. a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree issued by a university in the Netherlands; 

b. a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree issued by a university of applied sciences in the Netherlands, provided the degree program has English as the language of instruction or an English language test has been passed during the program, or if the program has Dutch as its language of instruction and English language proficiency is included in the intended learning outcomes of the program;

c. does not apply in this document.

3. Notwithstanding paragraph 2, as far as admission to a Research Master's program is concerned, a certificate as referred to in Article 2.19 is not required from a candidate who has:

a. a Bachelor's or Master's degree from a degree program issued by a university in the Netherlands, provided the degree program has English as the language of instruction.

b. a Bachelor's or Master's degree from a study program, issued by a university of applied sciences in the Netherlands, provided that the study program has English as its language of instruction or an English language test was passed during the program  demonstrating that the candidate has a sufficient command of the English language at the same level required in Article 2.19.

4. A certificate as referred to in Article 2.19 is also not required from a candidate who holds a Bachelor's or Master's degree from a degree program with English as the language of instruction. The student must submit supporting documents on the basis of which the student requests an exemption from submitting a certificate of English language proficiency.

Chapter 3.  Curriculum

Paragraph 1  Objectives and intended learning outcomes

Article 3.1  Objectives of the degree programs

1. The degree programs focus on:

  1. the academic education of the student, particularly with regard to the development of their academic thinking skills, their ability to form independent opinions and judgments, and their ability to perform and communicate at an academic level in speech and writing;
  2. the acquisition by the student of knowledge and skills in the relevant field and the formation of their character;
  3. the personal development of student and the promotion of their sense of social responsibility.

2. The Bachelor's programs are further aimed at preparing the student for a Master’s degree or career at an academic level.

3. The  Master's programs and Research Master's programs are further aimed at preparing the student for a career at an academic level.

4. Repealed.

Article 3.2  Intended learning outcomes of degree programs

1. In view of the objectives of the degree program, the knowledge, skills, and insights that the person completing the degree program should possess as intended learning outcomes are defined in the Degree program-specific appendices to these Regulations.

2. The intended learning outcomes are reflected in the learning objectives of educational units.

3. In accordance with these Regulations, the Examination Board establishes a framework for assessing whether the intended learning outcomes referred to in the first paragraph have been met.(33)

Paragraph 2  Content, design, and study load

Article 3.3  Content of degree programs and design of education

1. The educational units of the programs are divided per year of study into two educational periods consisting of semesters or four educational periods consisting of blocks. Furthermore, insofar as relevant, the educational units are divided per phase or track or as part of a minor or exchange. The educational units are sequentially described in Degree program-specific appendices to these Regulations.

2. For each degree program, it is always stated:

  1. the full-time, part-time, or dual design;
  2. the language of instruction;
  3. the total amount of free elective space, consisting of all educational units that have the characteristics of free electives.

3. For each educational unit, it is always stated:

  1. the form as a course, practical exercise including preparation for professional practice, internship or final work, such as the thesis;
  2. whether it is a fixed educational unit or a free or bound elective; 
  3. the study load, expressed in credits;
  4. the language of instruction;
  5. the code and name;
  6. for the practical exercises: whether participation is mandatory.

4. - 5. does not apply in this document.

Article 3.4  Further design of education
